 Summary Statement
 Obligation to provide a confidential report has been met and all initial reporting and compliance measures have been taken to comply with the Conflict of Interest Act .
 Exemption Granted Pursuant to Section 38
 In accordance with section 38 of the Conflict of Interest Act (the Act), Melanie Thibodeau, former Special Assistant, Regional Affairs at the Office of the Deputy Prime Minister, has been granted an exemption from their post-employment obligations under sections 35 and 37, insofar as it relates to accepting employment with the constituency office of Ginette Petitpas Taylor.
Ms. Thibodeau applied for the exemption from the application of post-employment obligations under sections 35 and 37 of the Act for a former reporting public office holder who was a member of ministerial staff who worked on average 15 hours or more a week. 
The exemption allows Ms. Thibodeau to accept employment with the constituency office of Ginette Petitpas Taylor. It also allows them to make representations on behalf of constituents to federal entities with which they had direct and significant official dealings during the period of one year immediately before their last day in office, to the extent that these representations are in relation to their duties and functions as an employee of the constituency office. 
In reviewing Ms. Thibodeau’s request, I considered all criteria listed under subsection 38(2) of the Act, which include the following:
a) the person was not a senior member of ministerial staff 
b) the person’s functions did not include the handling of files of a political or sensitive 
nature, such as confidential cabinet documents
c) the person had little influence, visibility or decision-making power in the office of a minister of the Crown or a minister of state
d) the person’s salary level was not commensurate with the person having an important role in that office
In light of the above, I have agreed to exempt Ms. Thibodeau of the post-employment obligations under sections 35 and 37 of the Act to allow them to engage in employment with the constituency office of Ginette Petitpas Taylor.
